children: Australian shares ended little changed on Monday as gains in financials offset losses in commodity stocks, while expectations of a central bank rate hike next week kept investors cautious.
ended flat at 8,731.90 points, after also closing little changed on Friday and losing 0.1% for the week.
Michele Bullock, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia, on Friday warned that upside risks to inflation are materialising from higher oil prices and the AI boom.
All the big four banks now expect the central bank to hike early next week as Commonwealth Bank of Australia
changed their forecasts. ANZ is pencilling in another hike in November.
The RBA will hike interest rate because of oil, sticky services inflation and Bullock's own language, said Mark Gardner, founder and CEO of MPC Markets.
"Our bias is still sticky, not cooling inflation, however, supply-side inflation (not demand-driven inflation) could cool the economy for the RBA,"
Swaps imply a 96% chance of a fourth hawkish move by the RBA this year to 4.6% at its meeting next week.
gained 0.6% with all the 'Big Four' banks advancing between 0.4% and 0.9%.
"Financials are catching a bid because the hike's now consensus, and a first hike still reads as a net-interest-margin gift," Gardner added.
dropped 11.7% to log its weakest session since late-August 2025, after it agreed to buy Germany-based ITM Isotope Technologies Munich SE for about $1.65 billion.
rose 0.5% as Brent crude stayed above $100 a barrel, despite falling nearly 2% on hopes for diplomacy in the Iran war.
rose 0.6% to 13,821.20 points, its highest since September 10.
